# PUBLIC Android image-list corpus

This encrypted database contains only data generated by Taypeer Android tests.
No user database, password, key file or external image was used. The SVG is an
inline synthetic green rectangle. No separate corpus licence has been assigned;
the project's licence remains an open roadmap item.

The fixed file is `seventy-image-entries.taypeer`, 4,567,715 bytes. Its SHA-256 is
`a965939a4ad83a973e93655d5b9ab435fd50c37c1acf08bfa6a4073985a3ea6d`.
Its deliberately public master password is `PUBLIC image list master`.
[manifest.json](manifest.json) records the origin and expected state;
[SHA256SUMS](SHA256SUMS) binds the ciphertext. This is experimental dev7, not a
stable release format or evidence of security acceptance.

- Container 1, archive layout 5, document 7, control 2, manifest/envelope 1.
- Automerge 0.7.4, as pinned in Cargo.lock. No local draft sidecar accompanies
  this corpus; the authenticated read-only verifier observes an empty collection.
- One root group named `PUBLIC image list group`; database name
  `PUBLIC image list visibility`.
- Seventy distinct active entries named `PUBLIC image 000` through
  `PUBLIC image 069`, all in that group, each with one saved history revision.
- Every entry and the group select a real local file image. The entries share
  one original image reference through actual Native cloning; the selected
  originals have the exact SVG below.
- The current and saved entry views contain no password, username, URL, notes,
  attributes, attachments, tags, expiration, foreground/background colour or
  field conflicts. The group has no parent or description.

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="32" height="16"><rect width="32" height="16" fill="#14dc28"/></svg>
```

## Origin and reproduction

The source was the actual Android
`ImageIconUiTest#eagerListLoadsOnlyVisibleNativeImagesAndRestoresThemWhenScrollingBack`
scenario in APK SHA-256
`9ed0801dd9b6d34359617530c039cdd334e3a44a014f323c83969472e65bb07b`.
It created and saved a group image, created and saved the first entry image, then
issued 69 public `DocumentSession.cloneEntry` calls with distinct synthetic
names. It used real encrypted storage, isolated workers and public Native
commands. It did not construct a fake overview, add a test-only model API or
replace production randomness.

[generator-reference.kt.txt](generator-reference.kt.txt) preserves that original
method before the UI regression adopts the fixed corpus. It is reference source,
not a second compiled test or a standalone program. For regeneration, restore
that method to `ImageIconUiTest` in an isolated checkout with its existing
fixtures and imports, and run on a dedicated PUBLIC emulator:

```sh
rtk proxy python3 apps/taypeer-android/qa.py test \
  --serial emulator-5558 \
  --output artifacts/android/public-eager-icons-regeneration \
  --timeout 1800 \
  --test-class dev.taypeer.ImageIconUiTest#eagerListLoadsOnlyVisibleNativeImagesAndRestoresThemWhenScrollingBack
```

The scenario generates the database inside that test profile; it does not export
it. The preserved method includes the original visibility assertions, so a
reader-performance failure after generation is not evidence of a failed Save.
Capture only the synthetic working copy from that dedicated test run, record its
identity and checksum, and authenticate it before proposing a new corpus. A
future generated file has new IDs, randomness and ciphertext; this command must
not overwrite the fixed file or update its checksum automatically.

The committed candidate originated in
`artifacts/android/parent-access-eager70-captured-public/candidate-public-seventy-icons.taypeer`
from the dedicated API36 16K test profile. Before promotion, the exact candidate
passed the hash-bound, read-only
[service verifier](../../../crates/taypeer-services/tests/android_public_eager_fixture.rs):

```sh
rtk cargo test --locked -p taypeer-services --test android_public_eager_fixture \
  captured_public_eager_fixture_is_authenticated_and_has_seventy_real_image_entries \
  -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The promotion audit read the original ignored artifact at its fixed path.
The current verifier runs by default against the committed corpus:

```sh
rtk cargo test --locked -p taypeer-services --test android_public_eager_fixture
```

It checks
size and SHA-256 before authentication, authenticates the archive, checks all 70
current/saved views and exact originals, and checks unchanged ciphertext and zero
writer calls after lock. It neither registers a device nor requests an author.
The fixed corpus is subsequently opened from a temporary copy in Android tests;
an independent, unadmitted local author has real read-only access.

## Purpose and limits

The corpus removes slow repeated clone preparation from the list-rendering
regression. It preserves 70 distinct saved objects, actual Native image pixels,
visibility gating, a 64-item cache bound, offscreen/revisit behavior and unchanged
ciphertext. Separate image acquisition and clone tests continue to exercise
their real write paths. Merely authenticating this corpus does not prove those UI
assertions, Android deadlines, worker lifetimes or Binder snapshot performance;
the instrumentation scenario must pass on the supported emulator matrix.
